title: Ohio's 7th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Ohio's 7th Congressional District pits first-term Republican incumbent Max Miller against Democratic nominee Brian Poindexter, a union ironworker and Brook Park city councilman. The district, which covers parts of Cuyahoga, Medina, Ashland, and Wayne counties, was redrawn in October 2025 under a bipartisan redistricting agreement. Cook Political Report rates the race as Solid Republican, giving Miller a strong advantage in a district that leans right. Key contrasts include Miller's background as a former senior advisor to President Donald Trump and his committee assignments on Ways & Means and Foreign Affairs, versus Poindexter's working-class, pro-union platform centered on workers' rights, affordable healthcare, and American manufacturing.
polling_note: No public opinion polls for the 2026 general election in OH-07 were found as of June 2026. Cook Political Report rates the race as Solid Republican.

candidates.name: Max Miller
candidates.summary: Max Miller is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Ohio's 7th Congressional District, first elected in 2022. A former senior advisor to President Donald Trump and Marine Corps Reserve veteran, he serves on the House Ways & Means Committee and the House Foreign Affairs Committee. Miller advanced unopposed in the Republican primary for reelection.

candidates.name: Brian Poindexter
candidates.summary: Brian Poindexter is a union ironworker and five-term Brook Park City Council at-large member who won the Democratic primary for Ohio's 7th Congressional District in May 2026 with 37% of the vote. He has been a member of Ironworkers Local 17 since 2007 and currently serves as an apprenticeship instructor. His campaign focuses on workers' rights, affordable healthcare, and bringing manufacturing jobs back to the United States.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polls exist for OH-07 in 2026, so this forecast is based entirely on structural and contextual indicators. Incumbent Max Miller (R) is a first-term representative with a strong conservative profile (former Trump senior advisor, Ways & Means and Foreign Affairs assignments) who advanced unopposed in the GOP primary. The district was redrawn in October 2025 under a bipartisan agreement, but Cook Political Report continues to rate it Solid Republican, indicating a lasting rightward lean. Democratic nominee Brian Poindexter is a credible challenger (union ironworker, five-term Brook Park councilman) but won his primary with only 37%, suggesting modest party-base enthusiasm. In the absence of polling and with a structurally Republican district, safe_r with ~95% Republican win probability is the most evidence-based rating. Confidence is medium due to the absence of polling and the recent redistricting, which could shift the district's precise partisan composition.
